title: Extinction rung — an addendum to the Auto-ARC incident ladder

provenance.requested_by: The project lead, 2026-09-16: fill out the far right of the severity axis -- the four incident curves should reach extinction, not stop at 1 billion deaths. The project team's 2026-09-15 request for extinction probabilities is met for the cross-cutting set by addendum-extinction-2026-09-15.json; this addendum extends the ladder itself.
provenance.wording: the question set's own ladder template, with the severity slot filled by 'human extinction (a reduction of the global population below 5,000)': the same 5,000 floor the XPT-worded pair uses, so the rung and the pair are the same event, and the rung inherits every ladder rule -- the cause's incident definition, substantial AI involvement, the elicitation-relative onset window and the three-year harm window. It has no dollar leg: no sum of direct losses is an extinction.
provenance.author: Drafted 2026-09-16 by the AIRO pipeline agent.
provenance.status: PENDING REVIEW by the question-set author. Project lead, 2026-09-16: if the author judges it wrong, the rung's forecasts are removed and re-elicited under the author's wording; forecasts made under this wording are retained under their protocol tag, never reinterpreted. First asked in the run of 2026-09-16 (17:00 UTC, by hand).
provenance.not_in_scope: No human anchor per cause: XPT asked extinction by engineered pathogen and by AI, not by cyber or by misalignment as this set defines them; those comparisons, if wanted, belong in data/human_baselines.json against the specific rung.
